subject: Workplace Skills
title: Single-Tasking Beats Multitasking
description: Learn Single-Tasking Beats Multitasking in one minute.

hook.text: Stanford research shows chronic multitaskers perform worse even when doing just one thing at a time.

buildup.text: Multitasking is actually rapid task-switching. Each switch burns glucose and degrades accuracy.

discovery.text: The switching cost is invisible. You feel busy but produce less quality work per hour than a single-tasker.

twist.text: People who believe they multitask well score worst on tests. Confidence and competence diverge sharply.

climax.text: Choose one task, set a timer, and refuse all other inputs until the timer ends. Start with 25 minutes.

punchline.text: One thing at a time. Every time. No exceptions.

quiz.question: What actually happens when people multitask?
options: The brain processes both tasks simultaneously
The brain rapidly switches between tasks with each switch costing energy
Only creative tasks suffer from multitasking
